To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the propagation properties of ultrasound pulse waves through cancellous bones are affected by the trabecular structure and that the variability of these properties can be quantified by the MILs of trabeculae and pores.

the propagation properties of the ultrasound wave in cancellous bone vary with the porosity and that the propagation properties are correlated with the microstructural parameters, MILs, of the trabeculae and pore spaces.

the propagation of the wave amplies and the speed of the wave propagation are correlated with the microstructural parameters of the trabeculae and the pore spaces, which are the mean intercept length of the trabecule and the pore spaces respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the numerical simulation of the ultrasound propagation in cancellous bone and the analysis of its variability due to the microstructural changes in cancellous bone.
the propagation of ultrasound pulses through cancellous bone models with a gradually increasing porosity.
the propagation of ultrasound pulses through a cancellous bone specimen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the variability in the propagation properties induced by the trabecular structure is mainly due to the changes in the pore space structure, but it is not due to the changes of the trabeculae.

the propagation properties of the ultrasound waves in cancellous bone are highly dependent on the trabecular orientation, and that the MILs of both trabecular elements (i.e., trabeculae) and pore spaces play a key role in the propagation of the waves through the cancellous structure.

the variability in the propagation properties induced by the cancellous bone microstructure is mainly determined by the MILs of pore spaces and the MIL ratio between the pore space and trabecular element.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the propagation properties of ultrasound waves in the oriented cancellous bone are strongly affected by the microstructural anisotropy of both the trabecular and pore structures.

the propagation properties of the ultrasound wave in the cancellous bone are significantly dependent on the microstructure, and that the MILs of both the trabecular element and pore space are effective parameters in describing the microstructure.

the propagation speed is mainly dependent on the trabecular structure and the propagation properties are strongly correlated to the MILs of trabecular elements, whereas the propagation amplitudes are mainly dependent on the pore structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the propagation properties of ultrasound waves through the cancellous bones with the same porosity are highly variable, depending on the trabecular structure.
the variability in the propagation properties is significantly dependent on the trabecular element MIL, whereas it is not dependent on the pore space MIL.

the propagation properties are strongly dependent on the microstructure of trabecular elements, and the variability in the propagation properties due to the trabechular microstructure is larger than that due to the pore space microstructure.
